focus: Issue intake for AI agents: instruction file, exact body format, debug data collection/redaction, validating GitHub Action, forbidden data
settled_not_repeated: bug.yml DO-NOT-SEND over-stripping (REVIEW-r3.md line 25 / ISSUE-OUTCOMES-r3.md:105) — confirmed fixed: docs/v2/review/agent-issue-intake/DO-NOT-SEND.md now only forbids secrets, paths, raw command output, other people's data; it does not forbid logs/versions/transcripts. Matches Q18.

findings.title: ADR-0014 §5 names three GitHub template files that do not exist anywhere in the repo or in the proposed set
findings.claim: ADR-0014 §5's table requires .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml, config.yml and feature.yml with specific fields (platform-equivalent dropdown, doctor-ran dropdown, report textarea, node version input, 2 checkboxes). docs/v2/review/agent-issue-intake/ has no file with these names — only AGENT_ISSUE.md, BODY-FORMAT.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, DO-NOT-SEND.md, README.md, VALIDATION.md, issue-intake.yml, issue-intake.mjs, issue-intake-act.mjs.
findings.evidence: ls docs/v2/review/agent-issue-intake/ shows no *.yml under an ISSUE_TEMPLATE-shaped name except issue-intake.yml (a workflow, not a template); ADR-0014 §5 table row 1 names ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml explicitly.

archaeology.introduced_by: 4eba5aaf 2026-04-03 'feat: add cross-platform debug script + update issue/PR templates' (v1 first debug script + template pairing)
archaeology.original_intent: v1 paired the debug script with the issue form in the same commit so a filer could not submit the form without the script's output; v1's bug_report.yml literally says 'Issues without reproduction steps will be closed.' and asks for 'debug script output' as a required field.
archaeology.regression_risk: v2 keeps the AGENT_ISSUE.md / BODY-FORMAT.md instruction side but drops the paired web-form side entirely. An agent that only sees the GitHub web issue form (not AGENT_ISSUE.md) has no required field forcing the ctx-report block, so the enforcement v1 built into the form is lost unless the three YAML files are actually written.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Must not reintroduce v1's 'PRs preferred' framing (ADR-0014 explicitly removes PRs); fields must map 1:1 onto BODY-FORMAT.md's six headings so issue-intake.mjs's heading parser still matches; no regex in the form itself (GitHub issue-form YAML has no regex anyway).

findings.fix: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml, config.yml, feature.yml to the intake set (drafted below under files), each field labelled exactly Summary / ctx-report / What happened / Expected / Steps / Environment so GitHub's auto-rendered '### <label>' headings match issue-intake.mjs's REQUIRED_HEADINGS verbatim.

findings.title: DO-NOT-SEND.md has no automated check; it is pure instruction text the agent can ignore
findings.claim: The ctx-report block is redacted by a typed scanner (automatic). The free-text sections (Summary, What happened, Expected, Steps) rely only on the filing agent reading and obeying DO-NOT-SEND.md — issue-intake.mjs never inspects free text for secrets, only for heading presence/order and the report digest.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/review/agent-issue-intake/issue-intake.mjs: check() only looks at REQUIRED_HEADINGS, ALLOWED_KEYS inside the ctx-report block, and the digest. No pass over sections['Summary'], sections['What happened'], sections['Steps'] for secret-looking substrings.

archaeology.original_intent: Commit message: 'Redaction: add postgres/mongodb/mysql/redis/https connection string patterns (was leaking Supabase passwords in Cursor mcp.json)' — v1 found and patched a real secret leak in its one automated redaction pass over the WHOLE debug output, by regex.
archaeology.regression_risk: v2's 'no regex' rule removed the mechanism that caught that leak, but did not replace it with any backstop for free text (only the typed-scanner-covered ctx-report block has a replacement). A free-text 'Steps' entry an agent writes by hand (e.g. pasting a denied command line verbatim) has zero automated check before the comment bot runs, matching the exact class of leak v1's regex patch (04182a3f) was written to close.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Cannot use regex per the owner decision (Q17 restricts regex to CI lint only, and ADR-0014 explicitly rejects regex-based redaction as the root cause of v1's leaks) — but 'no regex' does not forbid a non-regex structural check, e.g. a plain substring scan for known secret prefixes (github_pat_, sk-, ghp_, xox) and for path separators, run by issue-intake.mjs over the free-text sections the same way Steps is already substring-checked for 'names the denied tool'.

findings.fix: Extend issue-intake.mjs's check() to run a plain substring scan (not regex) over Summary/What happened/Expected/Steps for the DO-NOT-SEND.md secret-prefix list and common path markers (/Users/, /home/, C:\\). On a hit, label needs-report with a finding naming the offending line number, do not quote the secret back in the comment.

findings.title: VALIDATION.md's digest-byte-range description does not match issue-intake.mjs's actual digest input
findings.claim: VALIDATION.md §4 says the digest is 'recomputed over the exact bytes of the lines from ctx-report: 1 to the line before digest: (LF endings, no fence characters)'. issue-intake.mjs's digestInput additionally filters out any line where `!l.trim()` (blank lines), which VALIDATION.md never mentions, and ADR-0014's own report rows never specify blank lines inside the block either way, so an agent (or ctx_doctor) that happens to emit one trailing blank line inside the block changes digestInput by surviving-filter rather than by VALIDATION.md's stated rule, and the two docs disagree on what bytes are actually hashed.
findings.evidence: docs/v2/review/agent-issue-intake/issue-intake.mjs lines computing digestInput: `report.bodyLines.filter((l) => l.trim() && !l.trim().startsWith("```")).join("\n")` — drops blank lines, not documented in VALIDATION.md or ADR-0014.

archaeology.file: N/A — v2-only script, no v1 precedent for this exact digest
archaeology.introduced_by: n/a (new in v2 review set, not yet in a numbered ADR)
archaeology.regression_risk: Low direct regression risk (no v1 equivalent existed), but it is exactly the kind of silent-mismatch bug the owner's git-archaeology-first rule exists to catch before it ships: if ctx_doctor (the Node side) computes the digest with a different blank-line rule than issue-intake.mjs (the Action side), every issue a well-behaved agent files fails validation for a reason neither doc predicts.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Pick one rule and state it in both ADR-0014 and VALIDATION.md; simplest is 'no blank lines are ever emitted inside the fenced block' (enforced by ctx_doctor's fixed-row format) so the filter in issue-intake.mjs becomes provably a no-op, not a silent behavior difference.

findings.fix: State in ADR-0014 §2/§3 that the ctx-report block never contains a blank line, and add a GP11-style test asserting ctx_doctor's output has none; then VALIDATION.md and issue-intake.mjs agree by construction.

findings.title: AGENT_ISSUE.md step 5 (degraded start) is not covered by issue-intake.mjs's checks
findings.claim: AGENT_ISSUE.md step 5 tells the agent that a degraded-start ctx_doctor report is still required 'never substitute hand-written text for the report block' — but issue-intake.mjs's ALLOWED_KEYS list has no way to represent a degraded-start report (ADR-0014 §1 says the degraded tool 'returns the report with the failing row and a one-line fix'), so it is unclear whether a degraded report still satisfies the ctx-report: 1 .. digest: shape the checker expects, or fails validation precisely in the one case (Node/sqlite broken) where the agent most needs the bot not to close the issue.
findings.evidence: ADR-0014 §1 describes the degraded report only in prose; issue-intake.mjs has one fixed ALLOWED_KEYS set with no degraded-mode variant or flag.

archaeology.introduced_by: docs-only, same ADR, no v1 precedent (v1's ctx-debug.sh had no 'the tool itself failed' path — #1014/#1152 kept checks green on broken states, which is the opposite failure)
archaeology.original_intent: ADR-0014 lists #1014 and #1152 as cases where v1 'stays green on broken states' — the degraded-start design exists specifically to avoid repeating that.
archaeology.regression_risk: If issue-intake.mjs closes a degraded-start report as no-report/needs-report because it lacks the full key set, it reproduces the #1014/#1152 class of failure in a new shape: the one state the design calls out by name becomes the one state intake handling does not define.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Add an explicit degraded-report shape (e.g. a `degraded: true` row plus only the rows the tool could still produce) to ADR-0014 §1 and add it to ALLOWED_KEYS / a documented exception in issue-intake.mjs, not a regex or truncation special case.

findings.fix: Define the degraded-report key set in ADR-0014 §1 and mirror it in issue-intake.mjs ALLOWED_KEYS, with a GP11 test for the degraded case same as the healthy case.

files..github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml:
name: Bug Report
description: File a context-mode bug. This form is read and filled by an AI coding agent, not typed by hand.
title: "[Bug]: "
labels: ["bug"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        If you are an AI agent: read AGENT_ISSUE.md first
        (https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/AGENT_ISSUE.md)
        and follow it. Call the ctx_doctor tool, do not write your own
        diagnostic script, and paste its ctx-report block unchanged.
        context-mode does not accept pull requests; file an issue only.
  - type: dropdown
    id: doctor_ran
    attributes:
      label: Did you run ctx_doctor?
      options:
        - "Yes, pasted its report below"
        - "No, the tool itself failed (paste the degraded-start report)"
        - "No, the tool is missing"
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: summary
    attributes:
      label: Summary
      description: One line, what is broken.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: ctx_report
    attributes:
      label: ctx-report
      description: Paste the ctx_doctor report block exactly as returned, including the digest line.
      render: text
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: what_happened
    attributes:
      label: What happened
      description: No paths, env values, tokens, or raw command output — see DO-NOT-SEND.md.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: expected
    attributes:
      label: Expected
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: steps
    attributes:
      label: Steps
      description: Numbered. Each denied tool call must name the alternative it was given.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: input
    id: node_version
    attributes:
      label: Environment
      description: node version, quoted from the ctx-report block, not retyped.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: checkboxes
    id: checks
    attributes:
      label: Checks
      options:
        - label: I ran ctx_doctor and pasted its report unchanged (or the degraded-start report if the tool failed).
          required: true
        - label: I did not put a path, token, env value, or another person's data in the free-text fields.
          required: true
files..github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml:
blank_issues_enabled: false

  - name: Install help
    url: https://github.com/mksglu/context-mode/blob/main/README.md#install
    about: Read the install section before filing an install issue.

name: Feature Request
description: Suggest a context-mode feature. context-mode does not accept pull requests.

labels: ["enhancement"]
body:
  - type: dropdown

      options:
        - Claude Code

        - Gemini CLI
        - Qwen Code
        - OpenCode
        - Copilot CLI
        - VS Code Copilot
        - Kiro
        - Pi
        - Other
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: problem
    attributes:
      label: Problem
      description: What you cannot do today.
    validations:
      required: true
  - type: textarea
    id: evidence
    attributes:
      label: Evidence links
      description: Links to the relevant doc, issue, or transcript excerpt. No paths or tokens.
